tagline: E. coli engineered to sequester groundwater nitrate as cyanophycin, then flocculate so the nitrogen can be harvested back as fertilizer
summary: UOregon engineered E. coli to pull excess environmental nitrate into the nitrogen storage polymer cyanophycin and, once a cyanophycin threshold is reached, to express flocculation proteins so cells sink and can be harvested as a fertilizer substitute, closing the nitrogen loop. The target users are rural well owners and farmers in Oregon whose water is rarely tested. The education practice is the standout: three original curricula built for three audiences with increasing prior knowledge, developed through an explicit Design-Build-Test-Learn loop and grounded in Universal Design for Learning plus STEAM. The team also built an offline desktop search engine indexing the full text of 1,354 iGEM team wikis and 20,761 pages from 2022-2025.

dry.frameworks: Education itself was run as a DBTL engineering cycle, with a documented Reflective Theory of Change diagram and a standardised success rubric (engagement, science understanding, creativity), both adapted from an Oregon State University STEM Research Center presentation at the Polar STEAM Summit 2026. Learning objectives were written against the measurable verbs of Bloom's Taxonomy (Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create).
dry.dataviz: Hand-illustrated scientific diagrams throughout: all educational materials were digitally illustrated by hand by the team, including a central-dogma comic, illustrated workbooks, and illustrated synthetic-biology-tool cards used as a tactile matching activity.
dry.datascience: Post-workshop feedback surveys with section-level ranking; for Workshop 3, 8 of 15 respondents had heard of synthetic biology before attending, and bioethics and science communication ranked as the favourite sections, with the illustrated workbook, real-world examples and small-group discussions named the most effective learning tools.
dry.software: iGEM Wiki Search: a desktop application that searches the full text of 1,354 team wikis and 20,761 pages from the 2022-2025 competitions from a single search box, running offline with no server. It automates wiki collection and processing, builds a full-text index, ranks whole projects rather than individual pages, crawls responsibly, handles JavaScript-only wikis, and was tested cross-platform. The team benchmarked it explicitly against iGEM's Phoenix Project (metadata only) and iGEM Munich 2024's Data Explorer (2019 wikis only, no source links), and links every result back to its original page.

good.publicEngagement: UOregon's central design principle is quotable and transferable: 'Accessibility should lower the barrier of entry into complex science, not the complexity of the science itself.' Instead of one generic outreach talk, the team wrote three original curricula for three audiences with increasing prior knowledge and ran them as three DBTL iterations across June, July and October 2026, carrying the lessons of each into the next. Workshop 1 ('Intro to Synthetic Biology') was a one-hour session plus an illustrated take-home worksheet delivered to 30 high school students at the Oregon Humane Society summer camp; students reviewed the central dogma and plasmid parts and then designed their own engineered bacterium to solve a problem of their choosing. Post-event debriefs with students and camp staff produced four concrete fixes (establish prior knowledge first, add more real-world relevance, shorten transitions to reduce cognitive load, create more peer-interaction points), which were fed directly into Workshop 2. Workshop 2 ('Engineering SynBio Solutions') was a two-hour session for 20 high school students at SAIL (Student Academy to Inspire Learning), an existing University of Oregon STEM summer camp for students from diverse learning backgrounds; materials were a fully illustrated workbook, a hand-drawn comic that told the central dogma as a story, slides, and hands-on activities, with each of five sections framed by its own guiding question and sequenced to scaffold from foundational biology to CRISPR and plasmids to genetic circuits to experimental design. Workshop 3 ('SynBio Solutions to Real-World Problems') was a two-hour session for 20 first- and second-year undergraduate science students at the University of Oregon, funded by a University of Oregon Knight Campus Graduate Student Association outreach mini-grant; because this audience already had foundational biology, the team swapped the comic for a matching-game refresher, added directed evolution and de novo protein design alongside CRISPR and plasmids, and then extended into two sections the earlier workshops could not reach: small-group bioethics analysis of three real-world synthetic biology applications, and a science-communication activity in which students decorated tote bags to explain what they had learned to an audience of their own choosing. Evidence of impact is tied to the standardised rubric rather than headcount alone: engagement, understanding and creativity were tracked across iterations through direct post-workshop feedback forms and indirect observation, Workshop 2 students asked unprompted questions beyond the taught material (one asked whether CRISPR and plasmids could be used at once), and the Workshop 3 survey ranked bioethics and science communication highest. Beyond workshops, the team published a comic illustrating the AquaFlock project's journey and released the iGEM Wiki Search desktop tool specifically to make it easier for future teams to find and build on predecessors' work - an education contribution aimed at the iGEM community itself.
good.ihp: Human Practices was framed around rural equity: people living outside major cities receive less financial backing, less testing of wells and waterways, and less proactive healthcare, so the project is designed as a circular chain of agricultural, health and economic support for communities marginalised by municipal systems. The team mapped a four-step implementation path (in the home, then at the agricultural source, then harvest, then reduce/reuse/recycle) and stated the striking design goal that 'our product is made to eventually become obsolete' once nitrate levels fall out of the unsafe range. A field trip to the Metropolitan Wastewater Management Commission regional wastewater treatment facility serving Eugene and Springfield let the team interview plant operators, who confirmed nitrate control (alongside PFAS and silicon) is an unsolved challenge, validating a gap their smaller-scale system could fill. Four UN SDGs were adopted as focal areas: 3 (good health), 4 (quality education), 6 (clean water and sanitation) and 12 (responsible consumption and production).
good.realWorld: The intended users are rural Oregon well owners and farmers; harvested flocs become a local fertilizer substitute, localising fertilizer access and cutting nitrate at source. Context established on the description page: roughly half of applied nitrogen fertilizer is taken up by plants and the rest leaches as nitrate, driving eutrophication, harmful algal blooms and hypoxia as well as direct human health risk from contaminated drinking water.

gemsTakeaway: Run outreach as a DBTL cycle with a fixed success rubric: build three differentiated versions of the same curriculum for audiences at different prior-knowledge levels, debrief with the host staff after each delivery, and score every iteration on the same three criteria (engagement, understanding, creativity) so improvement is demonstrable rather than asserted.
